What this run shows about the strategy

Measured on this run's own baskets and fills; the numbers are in diagnostics.json.

1
38.4% of baskets win, and it needs 48.1% to break even
The average winner is $31.15, the average loser -$28.86: one average loss cancels 1 wins. The worst basket (-$424.39) cancels 14. The 10 worst baskets gave back 74% of everything the winners made. The margin over break-even is -9.7 points.
2
The ladder's big tiers fire together, at one price
33% of all ladder adds came within 3 seconds of the previous fill. By tier: M15 fired within 10 s of the add before it 79% of the time (median 2 s later, $0.13 per unit away); H1 fired within 10 s of the add before it 87% of the time (median 2 s later, $0.09 per unit away); H4 fired within 10 s of the add before it 89% of the time (median 2 s later, $0.12 per unit away). Those tiers carry most of the basket's size, so the 'averaging' is one large clip, not a ladder.
3
Full ladders: 29% win $181.03, the rest lose -$153.91
35 baskets reached all 6 positions; together they made -$2,037.39 (worst -$424.39). Baskets with no add made $22.28 in total; baskets with at least one add made -$2,026.67.
4
The slope exit closes losers near their worst price
69% of losing baskets were closed within 10% of the largest loss they ever showed. Losers were held a median 28 minutes (one in ten longer than 4.4 h, the longest 9.0 h); 67% of them had been in profit first. Winners were at worst -$272.71 under water before coming back.
5
Spread paid: $441.41
That is 11% of the gross profit of the winning baskets; before spread the run would have netted -$1,562.98 instead of -$2,004.39. Median spread at entry: $0.18 per unit.

Where the money came from, and where it went

While flat the bot polled 2,525,887 times: the open score wanted a trade but the force-close score vetoed it on 21.2% of those polls, the re-entry cooldown blocked a ready signal on 1.0%, and the trading window on 0.0%. A ladder tier hit its RSI level but was held back by the open-score gate on 12,504 polls; 343,542 polls were spent holding a full ladder.
